rfi.title: Nepal’s deadly glacier collapse exposes climate risks across the Himalayas
rfi.description: A massive glacier collapse that triggered deadly flooding on the Nepal-Tibet border has exposed the growing dangers facing the rapidly warming Himalayas, where scientists say retreating ice and thawing ground are making mountain landscapes increasingly unstable.

rfi.title: Haiti families plead for release of hostages after deadly gang attack
rfi.description: Families in Kenscoff near the Haitian capital Port-au-Prince are demanding the release of relatives taken hostage by armed gangs during last weekend's deadly attack on the town. At least 47 people were killed and more than 20 abducted, with thousands having fled their homes to avoid further attacks.

rfi.title: Former model sues French state over delay in Epstein recruiter rape investigation
rfi.description: A former model who accused an alleged recruiter for American sex offender Jeffrey Epstein of raping her in the 1990s is suing the French state for delays to the investigation. The state is also being sued by a child protection organisation, on behalf of alleged Epstein victims.

rfi.title: France to tie African development aid to efforts to limit migration to Mayotte
rfi.description: France plans to make its development aid to seven African countries conditional on greater cooperation in the fight against illegal immigration to the French island territory of Mayotte, as the issue becomes increasingly politicised ahead of the French presidential election next year.

rfi.title: Climate change is ‘very visible from space’, France's Sophie Adenot tells RFI
rfi.description: In an exclusive interview with RFI and sister TV channel France 24 from the International Space Station, French astronaut Sophie Adenot described the signs of climate change she can see from orbit and how she overcame major technical problems during her second spacewalk earlier this week.

rfi.title: Looking up: French sailors ditch GPS to rediscover celestial art of navigation
rfi.description: Astronaut Sophie Adenot made history this month as the first French woman to perform a spacewalk. Back on Earth, space enthusiasts across France are finding their own ways to reach for the stars. In the fourth of a five-part series, RFI meets amateur sailors learning to navigate by the stars, using a technique that allows them to find their position without GPS or onboard electronics.

rfi.title: Second person dies after man deliberately drives into crowd in Caen
rfi.description: A second person has died after a man deliberately drove his car into a group of people in the northern French city of Caen on Wednesday, leaving nine others injured.

rfi.title: Nigerian armed groups net nearly $6m in ransoms: study
rfi.description: Criminal groups in Nigeria raised nearly $6 million in ransom payments in the last year, a report said Wednesday, with two mass kidnappings by Boko Haram responsible for nearly 90 percent of the total.

rfi.title: France relaxes rules for three famous cheeses after summer drought
rfi.description: The drought in France is forcing farmers who produce milk for some of the country's most famous cheeses to feed their cows differently, as scorched pastures make it increasingly difficult to stick to strict rules on protected regional foods, known as AOP. Temporary exemptions on fodder sources will apply to the producers of Abondance, Beaufort and Comté to cope with the grass shortage.

rfi.title: Looking up: French collector gathers lunar photos that changed our view of space
rfi.description: Astronaut Sophie Adenot made history this month as the first French woman to perform a spacewalk. Back on Earth, space enthusiasts across France are finding their own ways to reach for the stars. In the last of a five-part series, space historian and collector Victor Martin-Malburet talks to RFI about his passion for Nasa's Moon missions and the photos they produced. He began searching around the world for original prints aged 15 and has now amassed a collection of 1,500 photographs.

rfi.title: French soldiers disciplined over Rhodesian flags linked to white supremacists

rfi.title: Looking up: Amateur meteorite hunters search for clues to origins of universe

zeit.description: Friedrich Merz hat bei RTL mehrere Bürger getroffen. Eine Kinderärztin warf ihm Bruch des Amtseids vor, eine Pfarrerin sorgte sich um den gesellschaftlichen Zusammenhalt.

zeit.title: Meteosat Third Generation Imager-2: Neuer europäischer Wettersatellit ins All gestartet
zeit.description: MTG-I2 soll Warnungen vor unter anderem Stürmen und Sturzfluten verbessern. Künftig soll der Satellit alle zweieinhalb Minuten eine neue Aufnahme an die Erde schicken.

france24fr.title: Les géants de la tech appellent à une "réponse mondiale" face aux cyberattaques aidées par l'IA
france24fr.description: Plus d'une centaine d’entreprises, dont OpenAI, Anthropic et Google, ont appelé jeudi gouvernements et entreprises à renforcer d'urgence la protection des infrastructures essentielles, face à des cyberattaques dopées par l’intelligence artificielle qu'elles prévoient "beaucoup plus répandues et sophistiquées" dans les prochains mois.

france24fr.title: Donald Trump signe un décret rebaptisant le lac Ontario en "lac d’Amérique"
france24fr.description: En pleine confrontation commerciale avec Ottawa, le président américain a signé jeudi un décret imposant aux États-Unis le nom de "lac d'Amérique" au lac Ontario, frontalier du Canada. Le Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney a aussitôt rejeté cette nouvelle appellation, qui ne bénéficie d’aucune reconnaissance internationale.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : les habitants de Kherson appelés à évacuer face à l'intensification des frappes russes
france24fr.description: Les autorités de Kherson ont appelé jeudi les habitants à quitter la ville située dans le sud de l'Ukraine, où les frappes russes visant les infrastructures essentielles s'intensifient, faisant craindre des coupures prolongées d'électricité et de chauffage.

france24fr.title: En RD Congo, les activités académiques dans les zones sous contrôle de l’AFC/M23 sont suspendues
france24fr.description: En RD Congo, le gouvernement congolais a annoncé la suspension des activités académiques dans les zones sous contrôle de l’AFC/M23, dans l’est du pays. Une mesure prise à quelques jours de la rentrée scolaire, et qui suscite de nombreuses réactions.

france24fr.title: "C'est le plus grand ambassadeur du basket français" : à Bercy, la folie Wemby
france24fr.description: Lors de la victoire contre la Slovénie (92-67) pour les qualifications de la Coupe du monde 2027, jeudi soir à Bercy, le nouveau capitaine de l'équipe de France, Victor Wembanyama, a pu mesurer son immense popularité. La star de la NBA est devenue la figure des Bleus. Un joueur aimé pour ses performances sportives, mais aussi pour sa personnalité atypique.

france24fr.title: Premier débat de la présidentielle 2027 : les principales propositions des candidats
france24fr.description: Jean-Luc Mélenchon, Marine Le Pen, Bruno Retailleau, Raphaël Glucksmann, Marine Tondelier, Gabriel Attal et Édouard Philippe ont échangé jeudi en clôture de l'université d'été du Medef, lors d'un premier débat en vue de la présidentielle 2027. France 24 revient sur les principales propositions économiques évoquées par les candidats.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Ligue des champions : PSG-Barça, Lens-City, Lille-Bayern... retrouvez le tirage complet
Ligue des champions : PSG-Barça, Lens-City, Lille-Bayern... retrouvez le tirage complet
france24fr.description: Double champion d'Europe, le PSG connaît désormais ses adversaires lors de la phase de ligue de la Ligue des champions, avec notamment le FC Barcelone et Manchester City au menu. Lens affrontera également les Citizens ainsi que Liverpool, tandis que Lille accueillera le Bayern Munich à Pierre-Mauroy et se rendra chez les champions anglais d'Arsenal.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : huit migrants tunisiens morts dans un naufrage en Méditerranée
france24fr.description: 🇹🇳 Douze migrants ont été retrouvés morts en Méditerranée après le naufrage d’une embarcation au large de la Tunisie. Parmi eux, huit ont été enterrées mercredi à Ben Gardane, près de la frontière libyenne.

france24fr.title: "La situation était devenue intenable" : pourquoi les FDS ont accepté leur dissolution en Syrie
france24fr.description: La dissolution des Forces démocratiques syriennes (FDS), prononcée mardi, marque un tournant majeur pour les Kurdes de Syrie, après plus d’une décennie d’autonomie militaire et politique. Retour sur les enjeux de l’accord conclu avec Damas et les raisons qui ont conduit Mazloum Abdi, le chef des forces kurdes, à accepter leur dissolution.

france24fr.title: Pakistan : les manifestations continuent dans l'Azad Cachemire malgré la répression et Internet coupé
france24fr.description: Des manifestations sévèrement réprimées secouent le Cachemire administré par le Pakistan depuis début juin. Elles ont notamment perturbé les élections législatives locales de juillet et d’août. Alors que l’accès à Internet a été coupé et que l'entrée des médias étrangers est restreinte, les habitants tentent de rendre compte de la situation sur le terrain.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027 : ce que les start-up attendent des candidats
france24fr.description: Le Medef veut du « courage » politique. À la Rencontre des entrepreneurs de France, son président Patrick Martin appelle les candidats à défendre davantage de liberté pour les entreprises, alors que le pessimisme domine chez les patrons. Mais qu’en est-il du côté des start-up et de la French Tech ? On en parle avec Julie Huguet, directrice de la Mission French Tech.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : à Ben Guerdane, les funérailles de huit migrants morts en mer
france24fr.description: À Ben Guerdane, ville tunisienne frontalière de la Libye, des habitants assistent aux funérailles de huit migrants morts en tentant de rejoindre l’Europe. Le bateau, qui transportait 15 migrants tunisiens, a coulé dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi au large de Zarzis, dans le sud-est de la Tunisie. Une personne a pu être secourue.

france24fr.title: "Le boucher de Bosnie" Ratko Mladic est mort, selon la télévision d'Etat serbe
france24fr.description: L'ex-chef militaire des Serbes de Bosnie Ratko Mladic, surnommé "Le boucher de Bosnie" pour son rôle dans le massacre de Srebrenica en 1995, est mort jeudi, a annoncé la chaîne de télévision publique serbe RTS.

france24fr.title: Au Sénégal, le pari d'un traitement contre la drépanocytose fabriqué en Afrique
france24fr.description: L'Afrique concentre près de 80 % de l'ensemble des cas de drépanocytose dans le monde. Aujourd'hui, le premier médicament générique fabriqué en Afrique pour traiter cette maladie fait naître l'espoir d'un meilleur traitement et d'une dépendance moindre vis-à-vis des médicaments onéreux importés d'Europe et d'Amérique.

france24fr.title: Crue meurtrière au Népal : le point sur la situation au lendemain du drame
france24fr.description: Plus de 1300 personnes, dont plusieurs centaines de touristes, sont portées disparues jeudi après les coulées de boue qui ont dévasté des vallées du Népal et de la région chinoise du Tibet, causant plus de 362 morts.

france24fr.title: Football : qui est Ayyoub Bouaddi, la nouvelle recrue de Manchester City ?
france24fr.description: ⚽️➡️Le club de Manchester City a recruté le Marocain Ayoub Bouaddi en provenance du Losc Lille. Le jeune milieu de terrain s’apprête à vivre une nouvelle aventure en Ligue 1 après s’être illustré avec les Lions de l’Atlas lors de la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.description: Dans une interview exclusive pour France 24, Sophie Adenot décrit depuis l’ISS les effets du changement climatique visibles depuis l'espace : une France plus sèche et jaunie en été, les fumées des incendies, des lacs qui s'assèchent et même des îles submergées.

spiegel.description: »Nur blutbeschmierte Kiesel sind noch übrig«: Augenzeugen schildern erschütternde Szenen aus den betroffenen Gebieten in Nepal und Tibet. Derweil erhöht sich die Zahl der Opfer weiter. Zahlreiche Deutsche werden vermisst.

spiegel.title: »GTA 6«-Video auf Netflix erschienen: 26 Minuten zum meisterwarteten Spiel des Jahres
spiegel.description: Rockstar Games hat auf Netflix sein bisher längstes Werbevideo zu »Grand Theft Auto VI« veröffentlicht. Es setzt voll aufs Gameplay und lässt erahnen: In Sachen Liebe zum Detail wird dieses Spiel Maßstäbe setzen.

spiegel.title: Frankreich-Wahlkampf: Sieben Bewerber ringen um Kurs in Wirtschaft und Migration
spiegel.description: Der französische Präsidentschaftswahlkampf nimmt Fahrt auf: Sieben Bewerber liefern sich erstmals einen Schlagabtausch. Es geht um Migration, die Staatsfinanzen und das Klima – und um die Nachfolge Macrons.

spiegel.title: Anthropic: US-KI-Konzern lockt Investoren mit 30-Billionen-Dollar-Markt
spiegel.description: Anthropic bereitet seinen Börsengang vor – und wirbt laut einem Zeitungsbericht mit einem gigantischen Marktpotenzial. Die Zahl verdeutlicht, wie ungebremst auch die KI-Unternehmen Nvidia, SpaceX oder OpenAI sind.

spiegel.title: Uli Hoeneß: Nachbar am Tegernsee klagt wegen zwei neu gepflanzten Bäumen
spiegel.description: Uli Hoeneß hat auf seinem Grundstück neue Bäume gepflanzt. Das gefällt seinem Nachbarn gar nicht, sie sollen gerichtlich entfernt werden. Hoeneß selbst vermutet dahinter »reine Schikane«.

spiegel.title: Österreich: 64-jähriger Wanderer stürzt in Vorarlberg 70 Meter in den Tod
spiegel.description: In Lech stürzte ein Wanderer rund 70 Meter einen Hang hinab. Die Notärzte konnten nur noch seinen Tod feststellen.

spiegel.title: USA: Demokraten warnen vor tödlichen Folgen von ICE-Elektro-Handschuhen
spiegel.description: Rund ein Dutzend demokratische Senatoren haben die amerikanische Behörde ICE aufgefordert, den Kauf von neuen Schock-Handschuhen zu stoppen. Sie warnen vor unverhältnismäßiger Gewalt und möglichen tödlichen Folgen.

spiegel.title: Sturzflut im Himalaya: Satellitenaufnahmen dokumentieren Schäden im Flutgebiet
spiegel.description: Wassermassen, die durch enge Bergtäler schießen: In der Grenzregion zwischen China und Nepal hat die Sturzflut zahlreiche Ortschaften entlang der Flussläufe schwer getroffen. Der grafische Überblick.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump überzeugt: Wladimir Putin werde »kein Nato-Territorium angreifen»
spiegel.description: Der US-Präsident spricht von »guten Gesprächen« mit Wladimir Putin und behauptet, dass Russland kein Nato-Land attackieren werde. US-Medien hatten zuvor berichtet, der CIA-Chef habe Moskau vor einer Eskalation gewarnt.

spiegel.title: Holocaustüberlebende Renate Aris: »Ich habe Angst, dass es wieder aus dem Ruder läuft«
spiegel.description: Als jüdisches Kind erlebte sie das Grauen der Nazis und überlebte den Holocaust nur durch großes Glück. Hier spricht Renate Aris über ihr bewegtes Leben, eine mögliche AfD-Regierung und sagt, was sie der Jugend rät.

spiegel.title: Champions-League-Auslosung: Bayern trifft auf Arsenal und Manchester United
spiegel.description: In der Ligaphase der Königsklasse hat Thierry Henry seinem Herzensclub Arsenal ein Auswärtsspiel in München beschert. Für Borussia Dortmund geht es zu Sabah SK. Die größten Namen hat RB Leipzig erwischt.

spiegel.title: Zum Tod von Ratko Mladić: Der Schlächter vom Balkan
spiegel.description: Als General der bosnischen Serbenarmee ließ er Sarajewo belagern. In Srebrenica beging seine Soldateska 1995 das schwerste Kriegsverbrechen in Europa seit dem Zweiten Weltkrieg. Jetzt ist Ratko Mladić im Gefängnis gestorben.

spiegel.title: Super-El-Niño: Die kommenden Monate werden die Klimazukunft der Erde sichtbar machen
spiegel.description: Der El Niño, der sich im Pazifik zusammenbraut, könnte Billionenschäden zur Folge haben. Ein Zusammenhang mit dem Klimawandel galt bisher als nicht belegt. Eine neue Studie könnte das ändern.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: US-Präsident unterschreibt Verordnung zur Umbenennung von Lake Ontario
spiegel.description: Erst war es der Golf von Mexiko, nun soll auch der Ontariosee einen neuen Namen bekommen. US-Präsident Donald Trump reagiert damit trotzig auf den Zollkonflikt mit Kanada.

observador.title: 2h. Carro de Luís Neves foi apreendido ao traficante "Xuxas"
observador.description: Volkswagen Golf GTD continua legalmente em nome do traficante. Advogado do traficante considera cedência abusiva e ilegal. Ainda, Benfica vence o Aarhus por 3-1 e garante lugar na Liga Europa.

observador.title: 1h. Segurança Social. Montenegro quer entendimento nacional
observador.description: Primeiro-ministro reforça compromisso de não fazer qualquer alteração na atual legislatura. Ainda nesta edição, União Europeia mobiliza um milhão de euros para ajudar vítimas da tragédia no Nepal.

observador.title: A silly season de São José Almeida
observador.description: É redondamente falso que exista em Portugal “um ensurdecedor silêncio e um real bloqueio da capacidade autocrítica de muitíssimos portugueses”, como São José Almeida garantiu.

observador.title: Podemos falar dos Estaleiros de Viana?
observador.description: Hoje os Estaleiros têm mais viabilidade económica, mas isso não significa que criem uma comunidade.

observador.title: Os governos de faz-de-conta
observador.description: Medo de fazer leis que se sabe que não vão ser cumpridas demonstradamente não há; revogações quando se sabe que a lei é letra morta ou que não se a quer cumprir também não.

observador.title: 00h. João Soares: comparar Carneiro a Ventura é "indecente"

observador.title: ONU: Proteger as nossas crianças não é negociável
observador.description: Não podemos permitir que opiniões burocráticas, desprovidas de voto democrático e disfarçadas de autoridade moral, venham ditar o rumo da legislação em Portugal.

observador.title: A Europa dos valores precisa de voltar às virtudes
observador.description: Os valores dizem-nos o que estimamos; as virtudes formam-nos para agir em conformidade, sobretudo quando isso custa.

observador.title: Bispos reuném-se com Papa e renovam convite para visita
observador.description: Audiência privada de cerca de 35 minutos no Vaticano. Virgílio Antunes diz que o diálogo foi "muito amistoso" e espera a visita do Papa "logo que possível".

observador.title: Farah Ahmed: quando o radicalismo muda de linguagem
observador.description: O caso Farah Ahmed não é importante por dizer respeito a Cambridge. É importante porque acontece em Cambridge.

observador.title: Família de Odair Moniz recorre e pede pena efetiva

observador.title: Montenegro vai à tomada de posse do Presidente são-tomense
observador.description: A deslocação, a 3 de setembro, serve também para preparar o mandato de Portugal como membro não permanente do Conselho de Segurança da ONU a partir de janeiro de 2027.

observador.title: Portugal executou o PRR. Quem ficou mais resiliente?
observador.description: A verdadeira medida do PRR não está no dinheiro que chegou ao Estado, mas na capacidade que deixou nas empresas e na economia quando esse dinheiro acabar.

observador.title: Cruz Vermelha Portuguesa pede apoio para vítimas das cheias
observador.description: A Cruz Vermelha Portuguesa abriu uma campanha de donativos para o Nepal, onde as cheias causaram centenas de mortes, destruíram infraestruturas e deixaram milhares sem acesso a ajuda humanitária.

observador.title: Trump assina ordem para criar "Lago América". Carney rejeita
observador.description: O primeiro-ministro canadiano destacou a etimologia indígena do nome, como forma de reforço da resposta a Trump. A mudança unilateral chega num aumento de tensões entre os dois países.

observador.title: Seguro felicita Pereira e Frazão por ouro em canoagem de mar

observador.title: O mito da sobreprodução e o resgate da nossa viticultura
observador.description: O valor da uva e do vinho português não se constrói com medidas paliativas, mas com a consolidação de regras inequívocas que tornem a autenticidade e a rastreabilidade obrigatórias em toda a cadeia

observador.title: O maior desafio das empresas familiares não é a sucessão.

phys-org.title: Videos capture humpback whales stopping to snack as they migrate along Australia's coast
phys-org.description: The southern humpback whale migration is in full swing. Tens of thousands of whales are now making their journey from warm Australian waters in the north to their cold feeding grounds in Antarctica.

phys-org.title: 'Mad honey' that can stop your heart is now being sold online worldwide
phys-org.description: A few months ago, a friend of mine told me that his father-in-law had been rushed to the hospital after eating some wild honey brought back from the hills of Nepal.

phys-org.title: Hitting bacteria hard and early with diverse phage cocktails may curb resistance
phys-org.description: As multidrug antibiotic resistance emerges as a potent public health challenge, medical science has renewed attention on the potential for bacteriophage therapy. Bacteriophages, or phages, are viruses that target, infect and replicate inside bacteria, destroying them in the process. To help maximize the success rate of this approach, researchers recently modeled the dynamics of bacteriophage therapy to explain particular therapies and optimize the composition of bacteriophage cocktails.

phys-org.title: Evolution favors flatter paths when fitness outcomes are equal, study finds
phys-org.description: A surprising discovery by Technion researchers sheds new light on the dynamics of evolution. Published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the study shows that when an organism has several evolutionary paths available with equal fitness, the path it follows is not necessarily chosen at random.

phys-org.title: Tiny oxygen gaps may determine whether next-generation memory films store data well
phys-org.description: Researchers have captured in real time the "birth moment" when the performance of a next-generation memory material is determined. The key lies in controlling oxygen vacancies, microscopic defects created when oxygen atoms are missing from their normal positions.

phys-org.title: Boosting soybean protein: Zinc and sulfur essential in sustainable crop production
phys-org.description: Soybean is a critical element of the global food supply: Between its use for animal feed and human consumption, it accounts for roughly two-thirds of plant-based protein meal output worldwide. Canada is a global leader in sustainable soybean production, with 70% of its crop, one of the country's top three by value, exported annually.

phys-org.title: Primed and ready to fight, a nematode pheromone arms plants to battle pathogens
phys-org.description: When cold and flu season comes around, we take steps like getting our flu shots and taking immune supplements to strengthen our bodies' defenses against pathogens. Plants face pathogenic threats, too. Plant pathogens can have devastating effects on crop yields, with up to 40% of global food crops lost annually, and such losses have severe implications for food security. phys-org.title: Vehicle-mounted spectroscopy system detects methane in real time
phys-org.description: Researchers have developed a vehicle-mounted spectroscopy system that can reliably detect methane in real time while driving. Using a moving vehicle to detect methane could make it easier to locate hidden methane emissions across large areas.

phys-org.title: Specific cover crops may help attract insects that target harmful pests
phys-org.description: Different cover crops may affect how plants defend themselves against pests—including by attracting more insects that eat harmful caterpillars—according to a new study led by researchers at Penn State's College of Agricultural Sciences.

phys-org.title: Discovery reveals rapid pathways to complex aromatic molecules in space
phys-org.description: A team of researchers led by the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa Department of Chemistry has uncovered a faster way large carbon-based molecules may form in space, helping solve a long-standing mystery about how some of the building blocks of the universe grow.

phys-org.title: Molecular makeover brightens organic light near 1,000 nanometers
phys-org.description: Near-infrared organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) that emit about 1,000 nanometers could support biomedical and security technologies. Yet pushing organic light to these longer wavelengths usually causes a steep drop in efficiency. As the energy gap becomes smaller, molecular vibrations more readily turn excited-state energy into heat rather than light.

phys-org.title: Study reveals inter-city collaboration on emission reduction boosts sustainability performance
phys-org.description: With Hong Kong recently recording record-breaking high temperatures, extreme weather has once again raised public awareness of global warming and emission-reduction measures. A large-scale international study led by The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) has revealed that intercity collaboration on emission reduction can improve overall sustainability performance by more than 10%. phys-org.title: AI model designs potentially stable protein sequences beyond those found in nature
phys-org.description: A protein's function is determined by its structure, and structure—the way a protein folds—is determined by its sequence of amino acids, the building blocks of proteins.

phys-org.title: Short, intense storms gain intensity across Hawaiʻi
phys-org.description: While long-term data show that Hawaiʻi is getting drier overall, short, intense downpours that cause sudden, dangerous flash floods are getting stronger on the islands, according to a new study by researchers at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

phys-org.title: Shear flow in narrow channels sparks amyloid formation, experiments reveal
phys-org.description: Many cars and not enough lanes is a recipe for traffic jams. Now, researchers from Japan show that even proteins can get backed up and start behaving poorly when too many try to squeeze too quickly through a small space.

phys-org.title: Heat-tolerant corals may be more vulnerable to disease
phys-org.description: Corals that partner with heat-tolerant algae may be better equipped to survive warming oceans—but that resilience comes with an unexpected trade-off, according to a new study from Boston University published in Science Advances.

phys-org.title: MOF-coated catalyst converts CO₂ to CO nearly five times faster under ultrasonic vibration
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Osaka have developed a catalyst that uses mechanical vibration to convert carbon dioxide (CO2) into carbon monoxide (CO), an important chemical feedstock. The catalyst consists of barium titanate (BaTiO3) coated with a metal-organic framework (MOF)—a porous material that captures and concentrates CO2 near the catalyst surface—and incorporates isolated copper (Cu) atoms as reaction sites.

phys-org.title: Mixture of traditional edible plants inhibits fungus growth in corn, study shows
phys-org.description: Fungal contamination in stored grain across sub-Saharan Africa causes major post-harvest losses and severe public health risks, costing billions of dollars annually, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). High humidity, warm temperatures and inadequate storage facilities can drive mold proliferation and toxin production in staple crops such as corn and sorghum.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

proj-syn.title: China’s Super-Dam Is Becoming an Upstream Water Bomb
proj-syn.description: The latest evidence suggests that the Chinese scientific establishment understands the dangers of a planned Himalayan dam—the world's largest—more clearly than its political leadership is willing to acknowledge. With the livelihoods of two billion people at stake, the international community needs to weigh in.

proj-syn.title: Europe and the War in Ukraine
proj-syn.description: If Europe remains a mere collection of small states and middle powers, the current period of profound geopolitical and historical change will also mark the end of its role on the world stage. With no end in sight for Russia's war in Ukraine, Europeans must come to grips with reality.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Stand with Canada Against Trump
proj-syn.description: Rather than keeping their heads down as US President Donald Trump wages another trade war with Canada, European leaders must recognize that they could be next. Like Canada, the European Union is a middle power whose future prosperity and security will depend on solidarity with economic peers.

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Champion of the Global South?
proj-syn.description: The United States is an overextended hegemon, and its decline will continue slowly, as other powers like China assume more global responsibilities. Against this backdrop, China’s efforts to lead the Global South are more about consolidating its power in the current international system than creating a new one that benefits all.

proj-syn.title: The Economist’s Embarrassing Proxy War Over AI Policy
proj-syn.description: The disagreements between the Nobel laureate economist Daron Acemoglu and his opponents are consequential—and so are the opponents. But rather than engage in good faith with Acemoglu's arguments, the venerable British news magazine recently stooped to bibulous calumny by unnamed critics of his work.

proj-syn.title: Democracies Must Get Serious About Industrial Policy
proj-syn.description: For decades, Western governments have ceded the strategic direction of their economies to the market. To dominate the industries of the future, they must learn from their own history and rebuild the institutions, expertise, and discipline that effective industrial policy demands.

proj-syn.title: In the AI Gold Rush, the Cloud Wins
proj-syn.description: Even if the AI investment boom turns out to have been a bubble, the Big Tech companies that have cornered the cloud infrastructure market will emerge as strong as ever, or even stronger. That is why Amazon, Microsoft, and Google are in a league of their own, even compared to other giants like Meta and Nvidia.

proj-syn.title: Don’t Mess With Markets
proj-syn.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has justified his intervention in currency and bond markets by arguing that they are not providing a fair signal of economic fundamentals. But they are, and Bessent's willingness to peddle such nonsense may be the most striking testament yet to the sycophancy that defines the Trump administration.

proj-syn.title: Kevin Warsh Owes Us an Apology
proj-syn.description: After only a few months in office, the chair of the US Federal Reserve has left market participants disoriented and confused. His first address to the annual monetary-policy symposium in Jackson Hole is an opportunity to set things aright—or to make matters even worse.

proj-syn.title: Is the Trump Treasury Panicking?
proj-syn.description: With the federal deficit near 6% of GDP and the national debt surpassing $40 trillion, America’s fiscal position looks increasingly precarious. By trying to strong-arm the bond market rather than address the underlying problem, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent may have squandered his hard-earned credibility.

proj-syn.title: What the World’s Oldest Bank Reveals About EU Financial Integration
proj-syn.description: To fend off an attempted takeover, Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena has launched its own bids for two other Italian banks. The episode shows why EU policymakers should focus less on making governments surrender their influence over national banking systems and more on building a European financing channel.

proj-syn.title: The Age of Gated Recessions
proj-syn.description: Aggregate economic indicators are obscuring a widening divide between those enjoying rapid income growth and those facing deteriorating job prospects. The rise of AI could deepen this disparity, with certain regions and workers experiencing recession-like conditions while others enjoy boom times.

proj-syn.title: The AI Curse
proj-syn.description: Every sanction that ordinary citizens have ever possessed—the ability to withhold labor, taxes, sons, or votes—presupposes someone who needs what you can withhold. As AI infrastructure encroaches on Americans, they are learning the lesson of many resource-rich states: where there is no need, there is no democracy.

proj-syn.title: Where Will the Global Bond Rout Hit Growth and Equities?
proj-syn.description: In the US, the recent rise in bond yields is largely driven by structural factors like the end of the post-2008 Great Stagnation, higher potential growth from tech-industry investments, and greater private-sector demand for credit. Higher yields are more worrisome for advanced economies that are stagnating and innovating less.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Korean Catastrophe
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump seems not to appreciate that deterrence depends on the ability to mount a credible defense. This makes the Korean Peninsula a more dangerous place, not least because 28,000 US troops are stationed in South Korea, which the US is obliged by treaty to defend.

proj-syn.title: The Dollar’s Outer Defenses Have Been Breached
proj-syn.description: The puzzle of why the Trump administration is so concerned with a falling yen has historical parallels not to the 1930s or the 1980s, but to the 1960s, when US officials feared that a crisis elsewhere could spread to America. With US bond yields spiking, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is getting desperate.

proj-syn.title: Why the World Still Needs Wall Street
proj-syn.description: Outside of the United States, all other financial systems face major constraints on their ability to absorb large financial inflows. That is why geopolitical multipolarity is advancing faster than financial multipolarity, despite the many reasons that investors have to pursue greater diversification.

proj-syn.title: Aging Populations Need Not Mean Frailer Economies
proj-syn.description: Governments and economists have long viewed demographic aging as a threat to economic growth. But new research finds that labor scarcity encourages investment and shifts innovation toward labor-saving technologies, boosting productivity enough to offset a shrinking workforce.
